title: Crosswalk
description:
A relation between the positions of two regimes. Kept out of the regime documents on purpose: a regime is a self-contained statement of one law, and must not depend on another regime to be read. A crosswalk is an editorial artefact with its own provenance and its own confidence, and deleting it must never change what a regime says.

Two kinds, and the difference is not cosmetic. An 'assimilation' is within one jurisdiction and has legal grounding - Article 32 of the draft requires every serving person to be reincadrat onto a position in the new annexes. An 'alignment' is between jurisdictions, is editorial, has no legal force whatsoever, and exists only to compare shape.

kind.description: assimilation: same jurisdiction, one regime superseding another, legally grounded. alignment: different jurisdictions, editorial, structural comparison only - never a claim that two posts are equivalent in pay, status or duties.

from.description: regime id the links start from

to.description: regime id the links point to

legalBasis.description: For kind = assimilation, the provision that mandates the exercise. Art. 32 alin. (1)-(2) of the draft. Absent for alignments, and its absence is meaningful.

authority.description: published: the mapping is itself an official table. reconstructed: inferred from two official documents. editorial: the authors' judgement. The Romanian assimilation is 'reconstructed' at best - Article 32 requires the reincadrare but publishes no mapping, leaving each ordonator to decide, so the same former title can land differently in two institutions.

needs.description: Source documents required to populate or finish this crosswalk. Lets a half-built crosswalk state what is missing instead of quietly looking complete.

relation.description: Cardinality is the point. merge: many from, one to - the dominant Romanian case. split: one from, many to. new: nothing on the 'from' side, so nobody is being reincadrat onto it. abolished: nothing on the 'to' side, which is the finding that matters most to the people holding it.

confidence.description: assumed links must never be shown without saying so. A crosswalk that quietly guesses is worse than no crosswalk, because it launders judgement as fact.

evidence.description: Why this link is believed: identical title, identical duties in the annex, identical code stem, same coefficient.

disputed.description: The link is contested, or two ordonatori are known to have resolved it differently.

proposedName.description: What the position would be called if it were named the way the labour market names jobs — occupation and level of expertise — instead of by employing institution and legal status. Present only where the two naming logics actually differ; a Romanian title that already reads like a labour-market title does not get one.

title.description: The specific title within that position, when the position carries several.

weight.description: Share of the endpoint's filled posts attributed to this link. Required whenever a merge or split is used in aggregate or envelope mode: collapsing four former titles into one new position only produces an honest wage-bill delta if the four headcounts are weighted. Absent means unknown, and the engine must refuse to aggregate rather than assume an even split.

evidence: Both former titles appear verbatim inside the new row's title cell.
